title: Spark Savings v2 instances bound risk with a supply cap and yield ceiling instead of conduit rate limits
content:
Two different risk vocabularies coexist in the same Artifact. Liquidity Layer conduits are governed by inflow/outflow `maxAmount` and `slope`. Spark Savings v2 instances are instead governed by a `Risk Parameters Current Configuration` block containing **supply cap**, **max yield**, and **current yield** — for example A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.2.1.4.2.1 (500,000,000 USDC cap, max yield 10%) and A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.6.1.1.4.2.1 (750,000,000 USDT cap, max yield 6%).

Crucially, the rate limits that *do* exist on these instances — `take` and `transferAssets` — are set to `maxAmount`: **Unlimited** (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.2.1.4.2.3, .4.2.4 and the X Layer equivalents at .3.6.1.1.4.2.3, .4.2.4).

The divergence follows from the direction of trust. A conduit pushes Sky's capital *into* a third-party protocol, so the risk is external and velocity-shaped — throttle it. A savings vault accepts *user* deposits into Spark's own contracts, so the risk is the size of the liability Spark has underwritten and the rate it has promised — cap the stock and cap the price.

The trade-off is explicit: with take and transferAssets unlimited, nothing rate-limits movement of vault assets by the authorized taker role. All of the protection sits in the supply cap and in the role-holder's key security, with no time-based circuit breaker behind them.
description: Where Liquidity Layer conduits use inflow/outflow maxAmount and slope, Savings v2 uses supply cap plus max yield, and leaves take and transferAssets rate limits Unlimited.
